description: Values shared verbatim between the Python engine (orchestrator/contract.py) and the HT bridge (bridge/extensions/orchestrator/*.ts, via the symlinked copy of this file). This is the on-disk layout and CLI wire contract: stream file names, protected file names, the durable-write CLI's exit codes and body statuses, batch/id limits, the path-redaction regexes and the state-root environment variables/default. It does NOT hold orchestration method vocabulary (capabilities, tiers, effort, roles) — that lives in method.json. Editing this file edits the on-disk contract for both runtimes at once; keep both sides' behaviour identical except where a field is explicitly documented as intentionally different (see redaction_regex).
max_leads_note: B4.7: the single source for the orchestration lead-count ceiling, consumed by orchestrator/scheduler.py's topology_for (which never requests more leads than this for any complexity/parallelizable input) and by the TS bridge's config.ts (the default for maxLeads, overridable per-run via HUMAIN_ORCHESTRATOR_MAX_LEADS). 4 was chosen to preserve the pre-B4.7 effective behaviour: the Python plan topology already capped itself at 4 leads, so the TS side's old default of 8 was never the binding constraint (config.ts's maxLeads is `min`'d against the plan's own leads, and the plan never exceeded 4) — no behaviour change for a normal /orchestrate run.

ingest_status._note: B4.7: single source for the ingest_status.json shape, built independently by two different writers on different failure paths — Python's orchestrator/ingest/service.py:make_ingest_status (a completed ingest sweep, which may be ok/partial/error) and the TS bridge's hooks/ingest.ts:recordHookFailure (a hook-level failure before/around a Python spawn, always 'error'). Both read field names and status-string literals from here instead of re-typing them, so the written JSON's keys and status vocabulary can never drift even though the two writers cover different scenarios and are not expected to share write logic.

redaction_regex._todo: these already differ in behaviour (python's character class excludes only space/tab/newline/pipe; ts's excludes any whitespace plus pipe) and are stored separately on purpose. DO NOT harmonize them here — that is a deliberate follow-up decision, not part of this refactor. Each side must keep importing exactly its own key.
